goal: Measure whether a charged offline one-variable-relocation order search can materially improve the exact final ROBDD over the frozen v0 fixed heuristics, and whether cheap vertex-separation width can safely prune relocation candidates without losing the best found ROBDD order. This is an offline order-search baseline, not CUDD dynamic sifting.

full_relocation.candidate_rule: At each iteration enumerate every distinct order obtainable by removing one variable from the current order and reinserting it at every position. Compile each candidate with the frozen balanced-pairwise ROBDD compiler. Pick the candidate with minimum final live nodes; ties by lower allocated nodes, then lexicographic order. Accept only a strict final-live-node improvement.

width_pruned_relocation.candidate_rule: Enumerate the same relocation neighborhood, compute exact vertex-separation width cheaply, retain every candidate whose width is at most current_width + 1, and compile only retained candidates. Same selection/tie-break/strict-improvement rule.

compiler.semantics: same positive monotone graph-2-CNF and exact ROBDD/rank compiler as coalition_boundary_width_pathology_v0
compiler.correctness: Every accepted final order must exactly reproduce the predecessor family rank vector and exhaustive truth function.

predeclared_interpretation: Improvement over the start order shows local relocation can recover value missed by the named fixed heuristic; improvement over the v0 best-fixed comparator shows the fixed heuristic panel itself missed a better tested order.
Search overhead is part of the cost and must not be hidden when comparing order control against no-search baselines.

If width-pruned search reaches the same final live-node count as full relocation with fewer compiled candidates, width is useful as a pruning feature on these cells. If it misses a better order, width-only pruning is falsified for that cell.
No result is evidence that this local search matches CUDD sifting/window/group-sifting or that it is globally optimal.
The graph-CNF rank-count experiment remains unrelated to global lemma-library promotion/demotion authority.

resource_guard.on_guard: retain partial exact results and label guarded_out; never infer local optimum from a guarded run
